transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time to meet. As you know, a student is scheduled to return to school next Monday after completing a three-day suspension following the cafeteria altercation. Before I can approve a return-to-school behavior plan, our re-entry policy requires me to gather current implementation information from classroom, counseling, and family-support staff. The plan also needs to address four key areas: supervision during unstructured periods, daily check-ins, extracurricular participation, and communication with the student's caregiver. I'd like to go around and hear from each of you on what you know and what's already in place so we can build a solid plan together. Who'd like to start?

transcript.text: I can start, Dr. Morgan. From the classroom side, I've been keeping working notes on the student's behavior during recent transitions. I have some specific observations and recommendations related to supervision during unstructured periods and daily check-ins that I think would be very relevant to this plan. Let me share those with the group now.

transcript.text: Thank you, Ms. Bell. I'd welcome hearing your observations on supervision and check-ins. From the counseling side, I have information relevant to the extracurricular participation component of the plan that I'd like to share with the group as well.

Based on those observations, I recommend an assigned-adult lunch table and a 30-minute morning check-in for the first five school days. I recorded this in my working notes but have not yet entered it in the behavior system.
